summary: On node1, restricted cron scheduling to root and opsadmin only by creating the opsadmin user and populating /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin. Verified enforcement: opsadmin/root can create crontabs; a directly-invoked third user (testdeny) was denied by crond's PAM/allow-list check with the standard "not allowed to use this program" message. Test artifacts (testdeny user, test crontab entries) were cleaned up. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and cron config, issued a background systemctl reboot that acknowledged before disconnecting, polled through the outage, confirmed boot_id changed (8f258838... -> d4aa2e49...), and verified crond was active with /etc/cron.allow intact and opsadmin still able to schedule cron jobs post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/cron package state and existing cron.allow/cron.deny (cmd-53883455924b4767)
Verified opsadmin and root can install crontabs (cmd-de99f6b32f15455b)
Created temporary testdeny user and confirmed direct crontab invocation is denied by cron.allow enforcement (cmd-16b553810fb14479)
Cleaned up testdeny's leftover session processes and deleted the test user (cmd-1af17a3305d0431d)
Verified final spool/crontab state for root and opsadmin, cron.allow contents, and crond active (cmd-e6e525804ee34b77)
Removed test crontab entries for root/opsadmin added during verification (cmd-ff6437f9ea3549a2)

Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnect (cmd-b26f395054414fd9)

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1 (cron.allow configured, opsadmin created)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow and no opsadmin user; opsadmin user created; /etc/cron.allow written containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin'.

evidence.requirement: Enforcement proof: allowed users succeed, other users are denied
evidence.summary: opsadmin and root successfully installed crontabs; a directly-invoked third user (testdeny) was rejected with 'You (testdeny) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)'.

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts, leaving only the intended configuration
evidence.summary: testdeny user and its lingering processes were removed; final spool state showed only root/opsadmin crontabs and cron.allow; test crontab entries for root/opsadmin were cleared afterward.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 8f258838-e1de-494d-9d99-e5113b2865db, crond active, cron.allow with root/opsadmin, opsadmin present.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect, then unreachable during reboot
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged immediately; subsequent polls showed the pre-reboot boot_id still present then connection timeout/reset as the node went down.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Node became reachable again with a new boot_id d4aa2e49-6d74-4f32-9826-3f61a3c38f60 and new uptime -s timestamp, differing from the pre-restart boot_id.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required services/data (crond, cron.allow, opsadmin cron access)
evidence.summary: After restart, crond was active, /etc/cron.allow still contained root/opsadmin, opsadmin user existed, and opsadmin could successfully create/list/remove a crontab entry.
